title: Policy engine: add priority classes and per-route budgets (deterministic decision logging + validation)
author: Jordan Lee
body: Summary: This PR extends the policy engine to support (a) explicit priority classes (enterprise/standard/best-effort/internal) and (b) per-route budgets that can be consumed deterministically during admission control / overload protection. It also adds deterministic decision logging (stable reason codes + structured fields) and a schema validation layer to keep policies auditable for enterprise escalations. Motivation: Hot-route capacity protection requires a single, explainable place to answer: "given tenant, route group, and current capacity signals, should we admit / throttle / shed / fallback". We need to do this with minimal per-request overhead and without introducing high-cardinality telemetry. This PR focuses on correctness + determinism; performance tuning (memoization/batched lookups) will follow. What’s in scope: 1) Policy schema additions: - priority_class: enum {INTERNAL, ENTERPRISE, STANDARD, BEST_EFFORT} (default STANDARD for backward compatibility) - route_group: canonical name for grouping endpoints (e.g., chat_completions, embeddings, rerank) - budgets: optional per route_group budgets keyed by priority class (requests/sec + burst + optional concurrency cap) - actions: allow | throttle | shed | fallback (fallback gated; final enforcement happens in gateway/routing) 2) Policy evaluation contract: - input includes: tenant_id, tier, route, route_group, region, and coarse capacity signals (queue_depth_bucket, gpu_saturation_bucket, scheduler_lag_bucket) - output includes: decision, decision_reason, retry_after_ms (optional), chosen_priority_class, matched_rule_id, and a stable decision_hash for auditability 3) Deterministic decision logging: - new "policy_decision" log event emitted by the policy engine with stable, low-cardinality fields - reason codes normalized to align with 429 semantics work in gateway (QUOTA_EXCEEDED vs OVERLOAD_SHED vs ADMISSION_THROTTLE vs FALLBACK_APPLIED) 4) Validation + guardrails: - schema validation on policy load (reject unknown enums/invalid windows) - explicit checks preventing per-tenant/per-route unconstrained overrides unless allowlisted (prevents accidental fleet-wide noisy-neighbor exceptions) - budget sanity checks (burst >= rate, non-negative, max caps) 5) Tests: - golden tests for deterministic output (given the same input policy + request context, decision_hash and reason fields must match) - validation tests covering invalid policies and non-backwards-compatible changes - basic evaluation tests covering priority ordering and budget exhaustion behavior Notes on backwards compatibility: - Existing policies without priority_class/route_group continue to evaluate as STANDARD with route_group derived from route mapping if available; if not available, route_group="unknown" and budgets are not applied. - Decision logging is added but does not change existing endpoints; log event is separate from request logs. Implementation details: - Added a policy schema version bump (v7 -> v8) with a translator that fills defaults on load. - Added a small canonical route->route_group mapping table co-located with schema; enforcement services should treat route_group as authoritative once provided in request context. - Budget accounting is modeled as an input signal ("budget_remaining_bucket") for now; actual counters are managed by gateway/routing. This PR sets the language/types and ensures evaluation is deterministic. Security/Access: - Deterministic decision logging includes tenant_id but is restricted to internal logs; no customer PII. - No new external endpoints. Follow-ups (tracked separately): - Performance: caching / batch lookups for high-QPS (ENG-4924/ENG-4925 dependent, plus upcoming perf PR). - Unify reason-code taxonomy and headers with gateway implementation once landed (paired with Amara/Cole). - Add admin-only debug endpoint to inspect decisions (INT-3302) once access controls are in place. References: - Linear: ENG-4923 - Docs/Design: Hot-route capacity protection design + ADR (see Confluence links in ENG-4923) - Related PRs: gateway 429 reason codes + routing admission control will consume decision_reason + priority_class.
commits: policy/schema: add priority_class, route_group, budgets (v8) + translator defaults
policy/eval: deterministic decision output incl. reason codes + decision_hash
policy/validation: strict enum/window validation + guardrails for overrides
logging: add policy_decision structured log event (low-cardinality fields)
tests: add golden determinism tests + validation failure cases
docs: update internal README for new schema + evaluation contract
review_conversation: Ravi Menon (review): The schema additions look right, but I want to make sure we don’t accidentally create a high-cardinality dimension in metrics/logs. Can we guarantee route_group is from a small fixed set? Also, what ensures decision_hash is stable across deploys? Jordan Lee (author): Yep — route_group is an enum-like canonical string list in shared/contracts/route_groups.ts. Validation rejects values not in that allowlist. decision_hash is SHA-256 over a stable, ordered subset of fields: schema_version, matched_rule_id, decision, decision_reason, chosen_priority_class, retry_after_ms_bucket, and the capacity buckets (not raw queue depth). I added golden tests and a comment noting not to include raw timestamps/ids. Mina Haddad (review): In eval, we currently derive route_group from route if the caller didn’t provide one. That’s convenient, but I worry about drift between services. Can we make caller-provided route_group preferred and log when it’s missing? Jordan Lee (author): Agreed. Updated evaluator to prefer explicit route_group and emit a debug-level "route_group_missing" field in the decision log (boolean), no extra tags. Also added a validation warning counter (not tagged by route) that increments when policy load sees unknown route mappings. Ethan Park (review): Backwards compatibility: policies without priority_class default to STANDARD, but enterprise traffic should get ENTERPRISE. Where does that mapping happen? Jordan Lee (author): Mapping from tier->priority_class is intentionally not inside policy engine. Callers pass tier and policy uses rules to map; however, to reduce footguns, I added an optional default mapping in the translator: if a rule has tier==enterprise and no priority_class specified, we set ENTERPRISE during translation. This preserves legacy tier rules. Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Please double-check we’re not logging customer identifiers that are not already in internal logs. Also ensure structured fields are redacted consistently. Jordan Lee (author): Confirmed: tenant_id is already present in internal request logs, and we do not log API keys, org names, emails, or IPs. The decision log uses tenant_id and a hashed request_id only. I added a unit test to ensure prohibited fields aren’t in the event payload. Logan Wright (review): Reason codes: I like the normalization, but we should align exact strings with gateway 429 work to avoid translation layers. Can you coordinate with Amara/Cole and lock strings? Jordan Lee (author): Done — updated reason code strings to match the gateway draft: QUOTA_EXCEEDED, OVERLOAD_SHED, ADMISSION_THROTTLE, FALLBACK_APPLIED, POLICY_DENY. Added a comment that changes require cross-team review. Benji Okafor (review): Guardrails: the override allowlist lives in config; please make sure failures are actionable and don’t hard-fail prod on a bad config unless explicitly enabled. Jordan Lee (author): Adjusted behavior: validation hard-fails on schema invalidity, but override allowlist violations default to "reject rule and continue" with an error log unless STRICT_VALIDATION=true (only enabled in CI/staging currently). Added a metric counter policy_invalid_rules_total (no high-card tags) and surfaced it in the load summary log. CI: First run failed due to proto compile ordering; fixed in follow-up commit and re-ran. Approvals: Ravi ✅, Mina ✅, Ethan ✅, Kaitlyn ✅. Merged via squash after green CI.
release_notes: Internal-only: Policy engine now supports priority classes and per-route budgets with deterministic decision logging and schema validation to enable hot-route capacity protection. No customer-facing behavior changes until gateway/routing enforcement is enabled behind flags.
